diagnostic_evidence.quote: be left and right, respectively, eigenvectors corresponding to $\lambda_j$

issues.failure_explanation: In Section 5, w^{(j)} and v^{(j)} are arbitrary left and right eigenvectors, so f_j=\|w^{(j)}\|\|v^{(j)}\| can be rescaled to any positive value. The claim f_j\ge1 and the error terms \epsilon(t,u), \epsilon(t) in Theorem onset, which are built from f_j/f_1, then have no definite meaning. The bounds hold only under the spectral-projector normalization w^{(j)}v^{(j)}=1 (rows of V^{-1}), which is never stated for these vectors.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require w^{(j)}v^{(j)}=1, e.g. take w^{(j)} as the row of V^{-1} paired with v^{(j)}. Then f_j\ge1 follows from |w v|\le\|w\|\|v\|.
issues.overall_effect: The precision bounds of Theorem onset, the onset criteria (epsilon<) and (epsilonc<), and statements such as f_j=1 for normal A are scale-dependent as written.
issues.title: f_j is ill-defined without the normalization w^{(j)}v^{(j)}=1
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard normalization restores every statement unchanged, with no new argument.
